original_card.question: Can the proposed P104 joint endpoint flags be realized by a chronological correction program with coefficients, dirty restoration and an affordable complete bill?
methods: Construct one side-correction word at an explicit chronological cut with the needed frames still available.
Derive a lower bound on the side correction and hosting costs that decides whether this channel can beat the selected budget.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An exact arbitrary-input identity, source/target frame availability and restoration at the chosen cut, plus the complete channel+correction+idle/hosting bill or an explicit favorable bound. The native channel alone is not a supplier. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the revision-6 family record and #2981 static joint flags, alongside the reviewed #1991 channel. #2981 is an author-checked source archive, not an independently validated executable correction or a refutation of program-level lifetime floors.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only. Read the named package and review before relying on its local evidence; this command is not its replay or supplier admission.

original_card.first_experiment: After checking live handoffs, pin one named collection from #2981 and attach acquisition/delivery times, source dependencies and coefficient requirements. Test legal access and arbitrary dirty restoration; price any completion against the full channel/endpoint/hosting allowance. Stop with the exact missing implication or a scoped counterexample rather than expanding the static cover census.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Completing an already realized changed channel tests a concrete construction opportunity, instead of refining the incumbent packing. A positive local result still needs global and all-size admission.
allowed_variations: One correction factorization, one chronological cut, or one explicit hosting obstruction.
A changed correction schedule with an updated full bill and native frame contract.
scope_change_triggers: Recompiling the already certified low-rank channel without closing a new obligation.
Treating a pending ancestor, local histogram or unpriced side correction as an admitted global supplier.
Repeating a correction or physical conversion already supplied by a pending follow-up without adding independent coverage or a different unresolved obligation.
Repeating the 208-flag static matching or calling a static nested cover a chronological correction program. Independent audit of that certificate is distinct and remains useful.

existing_checks.scope: PR #2981 reports static joint endpoint flags and a matching of 208 departure and arrival flags; archival intake is not independent verification.
existing_checks.remaining: Independent flag check and a chronological coefficient program with dirty restoration and a complete cost.

actual_scope: Answer #3669's first open question for present-head flag 0 (X0 -> Y34, basis head 232): price changed schedules that co-host the head at Y34's settling update (3369, the ADD that settles Y34's final X0 coefficient) while X0 still hosts it and is live. Build two explicit splices of the published #1991 word, run the published p104-native-channel validate() on each with six newly lowered native edges, and give the exact before/after bill (events, ADDs, transport occurrences, rank mass, paid H_r profile, native edges, per-register surcharge) ahead of the published I-G/2 tail add at 5759. Add the matching obstruction: with zero added non-private rank mass no order-preserving repair co-hosts at any of Y34's fifteen updates, and no relocation of the settling ADD to any of 926 of its 1,113 legal slots does either; by parity the surcharge floor there is 2.
scope_change_reason: #3669 proves the published word never co-hosts flag 0's basis head at a target update and leaves pricing a schedule change open; #3532/#3508 priced the analogous flag-1 / flag-43 repairs. This package cites #3669 without reprinting its chronology, and shows that flag 0 matches flag 1: its forced set is blocked at zero mass, so the repair costs two rank units on the channel prefix.
bottleneck_link: Unlike flag 43, the present-head obstruction on flag 0 is not a pure scheduling artefact in the order-preserving class: every order-preserving co-hosting repair needs at least two added rank units, and two natively validated repairs reach exactly that floor (R0 order-preserving +1 event/+1 transport/+2 rank; R1 relocated, 0 events/0 transports/+2 rank). Whether a zero-mass relocation exists after 3438 is left open. This does not supply I-G/2, a side correction or a supplier, and does not price event 5759.
stop_rule: Stop after one flag (0): one order-preserving repair R0 and one relocation R1, both natively validated and billed, plus the head closure and exact least-frame zero-mass sweep for every Y34 update and every relocation slot of the settling ADD. Do not reprint #3669's chronology, re-audit flags 1/9/43, touch side-correction bills, or assign an owner to event 5759.
evidence: Settling update 3369 (Y34 += D23/4, chart [95,502,16,32,2]) carries X0 (+1/2 after 2815/2998 cancel) to Y34's final coefficient; D23's row is written only at 2511 and 3625 and Y34 is never read. R0 retargets 3367 (D23 -> chart+head, rank 2), 3368 (Y34 -> chart+head, rank 2), relabels the 3369 chart to [95,502,16,32,2,232], inserts D23 drop rank 1 after it, and retargets 3500 (Y34 -> final, rank 2). R1 moves Y34's 3368/3369/3500 into D23's full window after 3624: Y34 [95,502,16,32]->FULL (rank 5), the ADD in FULL, Y34 FULL->final (rank 1). The published check_native.validate() passes on both (741 and 740 native edges, 208 adapters, 280 framed rows, 72 dirty helpers restored); independent replay gives 280/280 rows equal. Bill: R0 4059 events, 2624 ADDs, 1411 transports, rank mass 2370, profile delta -H1+3H2-H3, +2 on D23; R1 4058 events, 2624 ADDs, 1410 transports, rank mass 2370, delta -H3+H5, +2 on Y34; C untouched. Obstruction: all 280 non-private registers sit at their rank floor; the #3508 head closure blocks all fifteen Y34 updates (first obstruction at 3369 is Y33@3438); the exact least-frame sweep with C relaxed is infeasible for all fifteen order-preserving updates and for 926/1113 relocation slots (every slot before Y33's read at 3438), feasible for the remaining 187. Selected kappa unchanged.

open_questions.question: Is there a zero-added-mass co-hosting repair with flag 0's settling ADD relocated after 3438?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The relaxed least-frame sweep allows it; a construction would make flag 0's present-head obstruction a pure scheduling artefact like flag 43's, while a proof of impossibility would make the +2 floor global over relocations.
open_questions.first_step: Search for frames that place D23's post-3438 read charts inside final(Y34) while keeping X sources' initial frames and the private register's charts fixed.
open_questions.blocked_by: R1 sits in that window but still pays +2 on Y34; no zero-mass construction is attempted here.

open_questions.question: Which +2 repair is cheaper under the repository's actual per-rank weights?
open_questions.why_it_matters: R0 costs a+2b and R1 costs 2b under affine prices; R0's delta -H1+3H2-H3 and R1's -H3+H5 can change sign under non-affine H.
open_questions.first_step: Evaluate both deltas under the per-rank weights used by the selected channel bill.
